t.1.104.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There was a foremost man of the Yadus named Śūra, who was the father of Vasudeva. His daughter was named Pṛthā, unequalled in beauty on earth.
t.1.104.4: Appointed in her father's house to the honoring of gods and guests, she waited upon a fierce and dreadful brahmin of rigorous vows.
t.1.104.3: Because she was the firstborn, he, a friend acting in friendship, gave that maiden to the great-souled Kuntibhoja, who longed for the foremost favor.
t.1.104.5: With every effort she satisfied that fierce seer of rigorous self-discipline, whose resolve in dharma lay hidden, the one whom they know as Durvāsas.
t.1.104.2: The mighty one had earlier promised the firstborn of his own offspring to his childless cousin, the son of his father's sister, and so that valiant man gave her to him.
t.1.104.7: Whichever god you summon with this mantra, by the grace of that very god a son will be born to you.
t.1.104.6: Foreseeing the law that applies in times of distress, he gave her a mantra endowed with the power of conjuration, and the sage spoke to her as well.
t.1.104.8: Thus addressed by that brahmin, the glorious one, though still a maiden, then out of curiosity summoned the god Arka, the Sun.
t.1.104.9: She saw him approaching, Bhāskara, the sustainer of the worlds; and the maiden of faultless limbs, beholding that great wonder, was filled with amazement.
t.1.104.11: Wearing armor that was born with him, his face made radiant by earrings, a son was born, Karṇa, renowned in all the worlds.
t.1.104.10: Then Tapana, the Sun, whose work is to give light, placed an embryo in her. Then she bore a hero, the best of all who bear weapons: clad in armor, glorious, the offspring of a god, enveloped in splendor.
t.1.104.12: And that one of supreme splendour gave her back her maidenhood once more; and having given it, the best of givers then ascended to heaven.
t.1.104.14: Then the illustrious husband of Rādhā, the son of a sūta, together with his wife, took that abandoned child and made him his own son.
t.1.104.15: And the two of them gave that boy a name: "Since he was born with vasu, let him be Vasuṣeṇa."
t.1.104.13: Then, out of fear of her kinsfolk, Kuntī, concealing that transgression, cast into the water that boy who bore the auspicious marks.
t.1.104.16: As he grew, the strong youth applied himself diligently to all weapons, and the valiant one would worship Āditya until the sun's heat scorched his back.
t.1.104.17: At the time when that hero, true to his promise, sat murmuring his prayers, there was nothing the great-souled one would not give to the brāhmaṇas.
t.1.104.18: Indra, the sustainer of beings, of great splendour, having become a brāhmaṇa, asked him, by way of alms, for his earrings and his armour.
t.1.104.20: Śakra gave him a spear and, amazed, spoke these words: "Whichever one among gods, asuras, humans, gandharvas, serpents and rākṣasas you hurl it at in anger, he will cease to be by this spear."
t.1.104.19: Cutting from his own body the armor that streamed with blood, and cutting off his earrings, Karṇa, dejected, gave them away with joined palms.
t.1.104.21: Formerly, it is heard, his name was Vasuṣeṇa; then, by that deed, he became Vaikartana and Karṇa.
